quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Only if other cars are nearby.
Always. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
Only while you are making the move, not before.
Not needed if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do. Always signal before pulling away from the curb.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment depends on:

options.text: The type of drink—beer has less effect than wine.
The type of drink—wine has less effect than beer.
The type of drink—hard ciders and mixed drinks have more effect.
How much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol affect your driving. What matters is how much alcohol you have consumed, not what type it is.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you it is not safe to enter from your current direction. Turn around and find another way.

questions.question: The DMV requires your vision to be:

options.text: 20/20 or better in one or both eyes.
20/40 or better in one or both eyes.
20/60 or better in one or both eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: 20/40 or better in one or both eyes.
questions.explanation: You must have 20/40 or better vision in one or both eyes to get a driver license. You also need at least 110 degrees of side vision.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because drivers:

options.text: Drive too fast for the conditions.
Check their mirrors and blind spots regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for road conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what other cars are doing instead of the flagger's directions.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws and ignore the flagger.

questions.explanation: Always follow a flagger's directions in a construction zone. Ignoring them is against the law and dangerous.

questions.question: When driving near light rail vehicles, always:

options.text: Expect trains on any track at any time.
Pay attention and obey all signs and signals.
Be careful when turning across train tracks.

questions.explanation: Expect trains at any time. Obey all signs and signals. Look both ways before crossing tracks. Only cross if you have room to clear the tracks safely without stopping.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before making a right turn, move your car as far to the right as possible. Do not cut across other lanes to make any turn.

questions.question: How should you wear your seat belt's shoulder strap?
questions.explanation: Your shoulder and lap belts should be tight. The shoulder belt should go over your shoulder and across your chest. Never wear it behind your back or under your arm.

questions.question: When should you slow down when using a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Before you enter the exit ramp.
After you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same once you are on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: When using a freeway exit ramp, stay at your current speed until you move onto the ramp. Then slow down.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean?

options.text: You can stop long enough to unload packages.
You can stop only to avoid hitting other traffic.
You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop only to avoid hitting other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming up. Get ready to stop completely before you go forward.

questions.question: What is this sign warning you about?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: There are more cars on the road at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: It is harder to see at night. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people and cars are not visible from 500 feet away.

questions.question: Large vehicles can have blind spots that extend up to 200 feet directly behind them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend 200 feet behind them. Do not follow a large vehicle too closely. The driver cannot see you there.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, two drivers arrive at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two cars arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. Let them go first. Then you can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: When only the driver wears one.
When passengers wear them on long trips.
When everyone wears them on expressways.
When everyone in the car wears them every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When everyone in the car wears them every time.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a projectile and can hurt other people in the car.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving does not increase your chances of being in a crash.
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving distracts you and increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers your plan. Look for other drivers who may also move into your lane.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you of an upcoming intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to keep to the right of the upcoming divider.

questions.question: What can help you avoid emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Drive in the right lane only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without sudden braking. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into you.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to continue driving in your current direction.

questions.question: A green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow, if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from a private road, you should:

options.text: Blow your horn to warn cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly.
Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: Before changing lanes:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers. Look for other drivers who may also be moving into your lane.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. Your car will stop faster and you can still steer.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction, maintenance, or emergency work on the road.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should turn into:

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Avoid cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather. Change lanes only when necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange construction and maintenance signs warn drivers of work zones ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: When a driver's left arm is extended upward, what does this mean?
questions.explanation: A left arm extended upward means the driver plans to turn right. Adjust your driving if you see this signal.
